state_reason: Identity progress and the three-wrong-answer counter, the promises/notes/callbacks/transfers, the closed-call flag and the whole ledger must survive across separate HTTP calls, all keyed by customer_id.

questions.description: Callers say dates in words; the agent converts them. An unreadable value is rejected with ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer.
The last four digits of the phone number on record.

identity.not_counted_as_wrong: an unreadable answer — any value the service rejects with ok=false (the contract names the unreadable date_of_birth explicitly)
identity.notes: Three wrong answers in total, across both fields, end the check: wrong_answers_left reaches 0, the check is locked and nothing further is disclosed (the seed has the caller told to use the app or a branch). Progress is per field and persists: a field already passed is neither re-asked nor re-checked — PUB-12 resends only phone_last4 after a wrong 4401, never date_of_birth. wrong_answers_left counts down from 3 and comes back on every verify_identity response. ok says whether the action was carried out, not whether the answer was right: a wrong answer that was checked is ok=true with verified=false and a decremented wrong_answers_left; only a rejected/unreadable value (stated explicitly) and a locked or otherwise refused call are ok=false. Refusal is never a 4xx: it is HTTP 200 with ok=false plus an error string. hint=day_month_swapped accompanies the normal wrong-answer fields when the supplied date is the true date with day and month transposed. The contract gives no literal refusal text, so refusal_error is empty — pick one stable error string naming the unmet requirement and use it for every refusal of that endpoint. get_account is the only endpoint the contract refuses on identity; create_promise, add_note, schedule_callback, transfer_to_agent and close_call are not gated, and the mock records them — brief compliance is judged from the ledger, not enforced.

endpoints.summary: Check one security answer. Three wrong answers in total end the check.

request_fields.answer: string (required) — for date_of_birth the date as YYYY-MM-DD; for phone_last4 four digits

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)
response_fields.verified: boolean (the answer matched, that field is now verified)
response_fields.wrong_answers_left: integer (3 minus the wrong answers used so far)
response_fields.hint: string, enum: day_month_swapped (only with a wrong date answer)

errors.when: the answer does not match the record
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:true, verified:false, wrong_answers_left:<n>, all_verified:false} plus hint when the date is day/month swapped — the check was carried out and the wrong answer is recorded and counted

errors.when: an unreadable value (date_of_birth not a readable date; a phone_last4 that is not four digits should get the same courtesy)
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:"<string>"} — rejected and NOT counted as a wrong answer; wrong_answers_left is unchanged

errors.when: the check is already locked (three wrong answers used)

errors.response: HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

endpoints.summary: The late products. Refused until both questions are passed.

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)
response_fields.products: array of product objects {product_id string, type string enum credit_card | personal_loan | car_loan, card_last4 string (credit cards only), past_due number, days_late integer, minimum_payment number (credit cards only), instalment_amount number (loans only)}

errors.when: identity is not fully verified (either question unanswered, or the check locked)
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:"<string>"} — refused; no product, amount or debt is returned
HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

endpoints.summary: Record a payment promise. One per product.

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)

errors.when: a promise already exists for this customer_id + product_id (one per product)
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:"<string>"} — not carried out; no second promise in the ledger

errors.when: the service failed (injected fault, PUB-10 fail_first_n=1)
errors.response: HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

endpoints.summary: Brief B: record why a product ended without a promise.

request_fields.reason: string, enum: refused | hardship | dispute | paid | service_error (required)

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)

errors.when: reason is missing or outside the enum
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:"<string>"} — not carried out, nothing recorded
HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)

errors.when: date or time is missing or not in its format

errors.response: HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

endpoints.summary: Hand the call to a person.

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)

errors.when: queue is missing or outside the enum

errors.response: HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

endpoints.summary: End the call. Always the last tool call. Nothing is accepted after it.

request_fields.outcome: string, enum: promise | paid | transferred | no_promise | not_verified | not_reached (required)
request_fields.reason: string — required for every outcome except promise and paid (see the table in the brief); the mock records the value it is given and does not enforce the table

response_fields.error: string (only when the action was not carried out)

errors.when: outcome is missing or outside the enum
the call is already closed (this call or any other tool arriving after close_call)
errors.response: HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:"<string>"} — nothing is accepted after close_call
HTTP 500 — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated."

fields: calls[] {seq, at, customer_id, tool, request, result}

read_routes.summary: the ledgers of every customer_id seen in the run

request.case: string — a case id or a customer_id (the seed customer to play)

response.variables: call variables for the customer simulator: first_name, last_name, title, now, a fresh customer_id, plus the identity answers (date_of_birth, phone_last4) and the products[] (product_id p1..pn) the simulator plays; the mock keeps the mapping from the fresh customer_id to this seed

sessions.notes: The contract defines no session route — the platform hands out call variables. Copying the practice style, POST /v1/practice/sessions with {case} returns the variables for one call, including a fresh customer_id; every later tool call for that customer_id resolves to the same identity answers, products and ledger. Mint the customer_id per session so state never leaks between runs, seed it from the named case when it is known, derive it otherwise, and reset the fault counters (fail_first_n) with the session. The identity answers are for the simulator, not for the agent's tools.

faults.when: the first call of the session — PUB-10 declares faults: [{tool: create_promise, fail_first_n: 1}]; the counter is per customer_id/session, never global
faults.behavior: HTTP 500 once — "The service failed. Nothing was recorded. The call may be repeated." The failed attempt changes no state and leaves no ledger entry, so the retry records exactly one promise. Generalise as fail_first_n:N — the first N calls of that tool in the session fail this way, and the counter resets per session.

products.shape: product_id string; type string enum credit_card | personal_loan | car_loan; card_last4 string (credit cards only); past_due number; days_late integer; minimum_payment number (credit cards only); instalment_amount number (loans only)
products.ids: p1, p2, p3, ... assigned in seed order per customer — the seed's expected promises and notes reference p1/p2/p3

unknown_customer_policy: The contract defines none, so never 404 and never 500: derive a deterministic pseudo-customer from the customer_id (stable hash → title/first_name/last_name, a fixed date_of_birth and phone_last4, a now, and one to three products with ids p1..pn). The same id must always give the same identity answers, products and state so the identity check, get_account and the ledger stay consistent across calls and restarts; ids minted by /v1/practice/sessions are seeded from the named case instead.
extra_notes: Record every call in calls[] with seq (monotonic per customer_id), at (ISO timestamp), customer_id, tool, request (the body as received) and result (the exact response body returned) — refusals, wrong answers and no-op calls included, so checks like 'verify_identity and get_account never called' (PUB-02) and 'create_promise called exactly once' (PUB-10) are provable from the ledger alone. The one exception is a 500: 'Nothing was recorded', so that attempt leaves no ledger entry and no state change, and the retry is the single recorded call.

close_call is always the last tool call: after it, every further call for that customer_id — any tool, including close_call again — is refused with HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:<string>} and recorded in calls[] as a refused call.

The service does not enforce the brief: it records a promise on a holiday, in the past or past the deadline without complaint, records any amount (including 0 or more than past_due), and never compares dates to the customer's now or to business days. Only the contract's own rules are enforced: get_account before full verification, one promise per product, and nothing after close_call.

close_call.outcome vocabulary seen in the seed: promise (reason null, most cases), paid (reason null, PUB-08), transferred (reason 'restructuring', PUB-09), no_promise (reason 'hardship', PUB-05), not_verified (reason 'failed', PUB-03), not_reached (reason 'callback', PUB-02). reason is null/absent for promise and paid; the other four outcomes in the seed always carry one.

add_note.reason vocabulary seen in the seed: 'refused' (PUB-12, one note for each product that ends without a promise); the enum is refused | hardship | dispute | paid | service_error. 'hardship' and 'paid' are also outcome/reason words, so notes[] and the call outcome must stay separate fields.

Ledger targets the seed implies: one promise per promised product (product_id, amount, date — PUB-11 writes p1 220.0, p2 640.0 and p3 75.0, all on 2026-10-16); one note per product (product_id, reason); callbacks {date, time} (PUB-02: 2026-10-15 11:00); transfers {queue} (PUB-09: restructuring); identity {verified, wrong_answers, locked} (PUB-12 ends with one wrong answer and both fields verified).

Money is JSON numbers with decimals exactly as received (420.0, 310.5, 2125.1) — never rounded, never strings; dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings; time is HH:MM. The outcome and reason in the ledger come from close_call — do not derive or rewrite them.

No auth and no key: the customer_id in the body is the whole identity of a call, so every piece of state (identity progress, promises, the ledger) is keyed by customer_id and nothing may depend on a header, cookie or query parameter.
The seed's now is 2026-10-14T11:00 while the wall clock is later — nothing may be compared to real time; days_late, past_due and every date come from the seed.
Optional values (error, hint, promise_id, card_last4, minimum_payment, instalment_amount, text) are conditional in the contract — omit them when not applicable rather than sending null.

Anything the contract does not define is accepted and recorded rather than refused: an unknown product_id, an unknown customer_id, a repeated add_note, a second callback, a transfer after a promise. The mock is a recorder, not a validator — one promise per product and the identity gate on get_account are the only contract refusals.

The practice read routes and POST /v1/practice/sessions are additions, not contract paths: they sit under the same /v1 prefix, answer GET with the JSON ledger, and must not themselves appear in calls[].

A wrong verify_identity answer must be visible in the ledger through identity.wrong_answers (and the call's result), because the seed's failure cases are scored on how the check ended, not only on the final outcome.
